liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Alligator** (2 reviews): Reviewer says Alligator, New Potato Caboose and Viola Lee Blues were apparently knockout performances despite the sound; Per Deadbase III, this was the first Alligator, not played again until 5/5/67 [5][6]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 review): Viola Lee is the only part that sounds decent, and the rendition is very good [7]

## Setlist highlights

- Earliest performances in the archive: New Potato Caboose, Alligator [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1967-01-27.sbd.8762.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 69 min; rated 2.67/5 by 9 [1]
- **gd67-01-27.aud.hanno.16744.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 6 songs; 78 min; rated 3.3/5 by 47 [2]. Said about its sound: Sounds like a cheap handheld mono cassette recording; poor sound quality, though of historical value; Sound is nearly unlistenable, though Viola Lee Blues solos are mostly listenable; Overall sound is horrible and muddy [3][5][7]

## Around the show

- The setlist differs from deadlists and may come from any of three Avalon shows [1]
- Reviewer says Morning Dew and New Potato Caboose are note-for-note the same performances as on the circulating 10/22/67 show [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1967-01-27.sbd.8762.shnf**: transferred by unknown; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Identifier lists it as a soundboard, but eTree lists it as an audience recording [1]
- **gd67-01-27.aud.hanno.16744.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Uli Teute and H.B.; source: Audience [2]. Also: Audience tape, generation unknown, cleaned up and patched; transferred via Hanno Bunjes and Uli Teute; runs 67:40; Reviewer says a handheld mic and mono cassette recorder would have been state-of-the-art for taping then [2][4]
